t.6.103.1: But Rāma, beholding Maithilī standing at his side, bowed down in humility, began to speak, with anger lodged deep within his heart.
t.6.103.2: Here you are, good lady, won back by me after conquering the enemy in battle; what was to be accomplished through manly valour, that I have now brought about.
t.6.103.3: I have reached the end of my wrath; the outrage has been wiped clean. The insult and the enemy have both been uprooted by me at one and the same time.
t.6.103.4: Today my valor has been seen, today my toil has borne fruit; today, having fulfilled my vow, I am here once more master of myself.
t.6.103.5: You, who were carried off while alone by a fickle-minded rākṣasa, that misfortune brought about by fate has been overcome by me, a mere man.
t.6.103.6: He who does not wipe away, by his own vigor, the dishonor that has befallen him, what manly purpose is there for that man of feeble spirit?
t.6.103.7: The leaping across the ocean and the crushing of Laṅkā, that praiseworthy deed of Hanumān, has today borne its fruit.
t.6.103.8: Today the toil of Sugrīva and his army, who showed valor in battle and counseled me on what was beneficial, has borne its fruit.
t.6.103.9: Vibhīṣaṇa, my devoted follower, who abandoned his worthless brother and came to me of his own accord: today his toil has borne fruit.
t.6.103.10: As Rāma spoke these words in this manner, Sītā, her eyes wide open like a doe's, was flooded with tears.
t.6.103.11: But as Rāma looked upon her, his anger welled up once more, like that of a blazing fire drenched with abundant ghee.
t.6.103.12: Knitting a frown upon his face, his eyes glancing sidelong, he spoke harshly to Sītā in the midst of the monkeys and rākṣasas.
t.6.103.13: Whatever a man must do to wipe away an insult, all that has been done, O Sītā, in winning you back from the hand of the wrathful enemy.
t.6.103.15: Let it be known to you, and may good fortune be yours: this toil of battle, which has been crossed through the valour of my friends, was not undertaken by me for your sake.
t.6.103.14: They have been conquered, just as the southern quarter, unassailable to the world of living beings, was conquered by the sage Agastya, whose self was perfected by austerity.
t.6.103.17: You, whose conduct has fallen under suspicion, standing here before me, are deeply displeasing to me, like a lamp to one whose eyes are afflicted.
t.6.103.16: But this was done by me while guarding my conduct and warding off reproach in every way, and wiping away the stain upon my own illustrious lineage.
t.6.103.18: Therefore go, with my leave, wherever you wish, O daughter of Janaka; these ten directions lie open before you, O gentle lady, for I have no use for you.
t.6.103.19: For what man of spirit, born in a noble family, would take back a woman who has dwelt in another man's house, with a mind swayed by former affection?
t.6.103.20: You fell from Rāvaṇa's lap and were looked upon by him with a wicked eye; how could I, who claim descent from a great lineage, take you back again?
t.6.103.21: It was for that purpose that you were won back by me, and my glory has been restored by me. I have no attachment to you; go from here wherever you wish.
t.6.103.22: Thus has this been declared by me, O good lady, with my mind made up: set your thoughts on Lakṣmaṇa or on Bharata, as you please.
t.6.103.23: O Sītā, set your mind on Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, or on Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, or wherever your own happiness may lie.
t.6.103.24: For Rāvaṇa, having seen you, so divine in form and so enchanting, dwelling in his own house, would not have restrained himself for long, O Sītā.
t.6.103.25: Then Maithilī, whose ears deserved only pleasant words, heard that unpleasant speech from her beloved after so long a time. Trembling violently, she shed a flood of tears, like a creeper struck by the trunk of a lordly elephant.
